exact_rule_and_proof: At an operational starting mesh, retain any supplied total order by enumerating its finite cells as roots 1 through N. This mesh may itself be a geometric descendant: geometric generations and labels are never reset. Thus the richer original arbitrary finite input-mesh/order interface is retained.

Root r has identifier (r, empty word). Its vertices are ordered lexicographically by their real coordinates. At a split, the earlier reference-edge endpoint in the stored list determines child zero, the other endpoint determines child one; both children retain the opposite vertex and the new midpoint. Their lists keep the two retained vertices in prior order, then append the midpoint.

Append the corresponding zero/one bit to the parent address. A different root or binary path gives a different identifier by finite-string uniqueness. Comparing root rank then lexicographic word with proper prefixes first is a total order. Every nonempty finite pending set therefore has a unique least element; no well-order on an infinite address set is required.

The construction commutes with request scheduling: a child address and vertex list depend only on its unique parent and reference edge. Retained cells keep their IDs across calls; simultaneous compatible partners compute child IDs from separate unique parents. No repeated address can be generated in a forest whose split leaf is removed.

Failed budget calls discard tentative splits and descendant IDs, so retry uses the same ordered input forest. Since a full finite request terminates independently of processing order, the same deterministic successful run has a finite bisection count and budget doubling eventually reaches it.

The curved seed has two different triangle vertex sets in the four indexed corners. Sorting each site-index triple and comparing the two triples assigns distinct root ranks without changing any reference-edge label or the square diagonal. Stored vertex orders are bookkeeping only and do not replace positive-orientation affine reference maps.

Whole common faces restore the exact published matching-simplex convention: in two dimensions a nonempty cell intersection may be a vertex or an edge. The bisection rule, shared labels and geometric descendant family otherwise remain exactly as intended. No claim or scope is narrowed.
